02 · Evaluation workflow

From predictions to a decision

1

Predict

Generate labels and survival probabilities.

2

Count

Build the confusion matrix: TP, TN, FP, FN.

3

Measure

Calculate complementary classification metrics.

4

Stress-test

Check folds, thresholds, groups, and error patterns.

5

Decide

Select a model and explain the tradeoff.

Evaluation is a loop: errors suggest a new feature, cleaning decision, threshold, or model — then we validate again.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIIPredict → inspect → improve

03 · Two model outputs

A label answers. A probability expresses confidence.

predict()0 or 1

Hard label

Used by Accuracy, Precision, Recall, Specificity, F1, and the confusion matrix.

predict_proba()0.00 → 1.00

Probability

Used by thresholds, ROC-AUC, Average Precision, Log Loss, Brier Score, and calibration.

Default rule: probability ≥ 0.50 becomes class 1. The threshold is a decision, not a law.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIIConfidence enables deeper evaluation

04 · The foundation

Every classification metric starts here

Positive class = Survived
Predicted 0
Predicted 1
Actual 0
TNCorrect non-survivor
FPPredicted survival incorrectly
Actual 1
FNMissed a survivor
TPCorrect survivor

Correct: TP + TN
Errors: FP + FN

False positiveThe model says “survived,” but the passenger did not.
False negativeThe model says “did not survive,” but the passenger did.
First question: are FP and FN equally costly for the real problem?
kaggle · Titanic Part IIICount errors before summarizing them

05 · Overall correctness

Accuracy is useful — with context

Accuracy

How often was the model correct overall?

(TP + TN) / ALL

Good when classes and error costs are reasonably balanced.

Balanced Accuracy

How well did the model perform across both classes?

(Recall + Specificity) / 2

More informative when one class is much more common.

Majority baseline: always predicting “did not survive” is already about 62% accurate on the Titanic training data.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIIAlways compare against a baseline

06 · Positive-class metrics

Precision and Recall answer different questions

Precision

Of predicted survivors, how many truly survived?

TP / (TP + FP)

High precision: few false survival predictions.
Recall

Of all actual survivors, how many did we find?

TP / (TP + FN)

High recall: few survivors were missed.
Tradeoff: lowering the threshold usually raises Recall and lowers Precision; raising it usually does the opposite.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIIPrecision controls FP · Recall controls FN

07 · Complementary summaries

Measure the negative class and the balance

Specificity

Of all non-survivors, how many did we correctly reject?

TN / (TN + FP)

Also called the True Negative Rate.

F1 Score

What single score balances Precision and Recall?

2 × (P × R) / (P + R)

Useful when both FP and FN matter and the positive class is important.

Advanced robust summary: Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) uses all four confusion-matrix cells and remains informative under imbalance.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIINo metric is universally “best”

09 · Decision threshold

The same model can make different decisions

Default = 0.50
More predicted survivors
↑ Recall · ↓ PrecisionDecision boundaryFewer predicted survivors
↑ Precision · ↓ Recall

Threshold 0.30

More positive predictions. Useful when missing a positive is costly.

Threshold 0.50

Common default. It is not automatically the optimal operating point.

Threshold 0.70

Fewer positive predictions. Useful when false positives are costly.

Choose the threshold on validation data using a stated objective. Never tune it against hidden Kaggle answers.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIIModel probability + policy threshold

10 · Ranking quality

ROC-AUC checks every threshold

Higher is better

ROC curve: Recall versus False Positive Rate across thresholds.

0.50Random ranking
1.00Perfect ranking
Caution: ROC-AUC can look optimistic when the positive class is extremely rare.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIIAUC measures ranking, not calibration

11 · Positive-class performance

Precision–Recall focuses on the positives

Average Precision

PR curve: shows how Precision changes as Recall increases.

Average Precision (AP)Summarizes the curve; higher is better.
Best useWhen positives are rare or positive-class performance is central.
BaselineThe positive-class prevalence, not always 0.50.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIIPR exposes positive-class tradeoffs

12 · Probability evaluation

Are the probabilities honest?

Log Loss

Penalizes confident mistakes

A wrong prediction at 0.99 confidence hurts far more than one at 0.55.

↓ Lower is better
Brier Score

Squared probability error

Measures the average squared gap between probability and the 0/1 outcome.

↓ Lower is better
Calibration

Confidence matches reality

Among passengers predicted near 0.70, roughly 70% should be positive.

Closer to diagonal is better
Important: a model can rank passengers well (high AUC) while producing poorly calibrated probabilities.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIIClassification quality ≠ probability quality

14 · Generalization

Compare training and validation

The gap matters

■ Train   ■ Validation

UnderfittingBoth scores are low: model or features are too simple.
Healthy fitBoth scores are useful and the gap is small.
OverfittingTraining is high, validation drops: the model memorized details.
Learning curveShows whether more data may improve generalization.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIIOptimize unseen performance

15 · Responsible evaluation

An average can hide weak groups

Inspect, do not assume

Calculate metrics for meaningful groups such as Sex and Pclass.

CoverageIs every group large enough to interpret?
Error ratesDo FP or FN rates differ sharply?
Data qualityIs missingness concentrated in one group?
Small groups are noisy: always report their sample size with the metric.

16 · Kaggle evaluation

Public feedback is not the final answer

Public leaderboard Visible now

1Model C0.806
2Model A0.799
3Model B0.792

Uses only part of the hidden answers and gives iterative feedback.

Private leaderboard Final

1Model A0.803
2Model B0.795
3Model C0.781

Uses the remaining hidden answers and determines the final ranking.

Leaderboard overfitting: repeated choices based on the public score can make you specialize to that subset. Trust cross-validation and limit submissions.
kaggle · Titanic Part IIILocal validation first · leaderboard second
